quest.title: Until the End of the World
quest.description:
"When that time comes, I shall dance, and return the tracks beneath my people's feet back to the stars in the sky..."

Thus would the epics of later generations speak of this time:
The heroes gazed upon the skies of gray, and in carriages bright they went their way. The stars returned and the winds they drove — now the dragon's shadow alone still did rove.
Comment in the margins: I feel that the young nekomata lady in boots who spoke the human tongue needs a line or two!
Comment below the comment: I'll make up for that another day... But really, what did you put into my cup?
Comment below the comment below the comment: I dunno, it wasn't me.
Comment below the comment below the comment: Wasn't me either.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.num: Summertide Scales and Tales: Page III
chapter.title: Until the End of the World

talks.objective: Wait until morning the next day (08:00 – 12:00)
Go to Constellation Metropole Station

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Carriage inspection, check... Wheel and axle inspection, check... power inspection...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Good morning, Mr. Wheel!

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Good morning, heroes of Simulanka.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, our old friend Wheel is the driver again! That already puts Paimon at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Are you certain you don't want us to accompany you, Your Majesty?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #I am. You can leave the dragon-slaying to us. My partner's a pro, {M#he}{F#she} does it all the time!

response.speaker: Bizerte
response.text: What remarkable friends Her Majesty has. With such great heroes by your side, I'm sure you'll best the dragon with ease. We won't keep you any longer.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, then! Look after the city for me while I'm gone.

response.speaker: Montagne
response.text: Yes, Your Majesty.

response.speaker: Bizerte
response.text: Just leave it to us.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I think we're all set. Time to depart.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Next stop, the end of the world!

choices.text: I've only fought two or three...

talks.objective: Go to Constellation Metropole Station
Ride the Maritime Express to the end of the world
Arrive at the transfer station and change trains

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: So we've got to switch trains, right? ...Huh? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like... Hilichurls! They've taken over that platform!

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Huh!? Wh—What do we do...?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Just find somewhere to hide, Mr. Wheel. We'll take care of them!

talks.objective: Defeat the monsters and connect the train carriages
Talk to the conductor and prepare to depart

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Phew. That's all of them.

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Thank you so much for your help, everyone. Now let me take a look at the train...

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Hmm, the carriage is a little scratched up, but there doesn't seem to be any real damage, and the engine is still operating normally. I think we're good to go.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Wonderful! Let's keep going, then.

talks.objective: Continue riding the Maritime Express to the end of the world
Continue riding the Maritime Express to the end of the world

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So that's why you took the stars... Because you missed your mom.

talks.objective: Continue riding the Maritime Express to the end of the world
Talk to everyone

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Are you okay, Miss Nilou?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #I'm fine, but I think {NICKNAME} is still unconscious...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We're lucky this guy caught us on the way down!
Hmph, passed out from a little fall, did you? How fragile...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Ah, cut him some slack. {NICKNAME}'s had a rough few days, we should just let {M#him}{F#her} nap for a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Uh? But my... my leg's falling asleep...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #You couldn't have set {M#him}{F#her} down on the grass over there, Hat Guy?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hah... I go out of my way to save four people who fall out of the sky, and now you're nitpicking my choice of soft landing? That's the most ridiculous thing I've ever heard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ah, {M#he}{F#she}'s awake!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Morning, sunshine. You were having a nice little dream there, weren't you? Not gonna lie, it was kind of adorable.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: You and your friends fell from the top of that waterfall, and you passed out along the way. Guess someone couldn't keep it together...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Sorry to break it to you, but crashing into the ground doesn't take you to another world. That kind of thing only happens in those stupid light novels they sell in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, he kind of set you down on Nilou's lap. So, that's where you've been napping all this time.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: P—Paimon!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Sorry...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Oh, no... It's alright... I—I'm just glad you're okay.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You didn't hit your head, did you? Is the dizziness gone?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Really? What did they say?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: The fog you see around here can have <color=#00E1FFFF>a hallucinatory effect</color>. Apparently, it's the work of that dragon. Maybe you inhaled some while you were freaking out on your way down...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #Uh, {NICKNAME}, Nilou... Do you know this Hat Guy person?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Oh, yeah. He's a student at the Akademiya. We met during the last Interdarshan Championship. He was representing the Vahumana Darshan.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, then... Hello there, friend! I'm Navia, the President of Spina di Rosula. It's very nice to meet you. So, should I just call you Hat Guy as well? Seems like that's what everyone's calling you.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Sure, whatever.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Wait, Hat Guy, what's that sword around your waist?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Tch, an unwelcome encumbrance, that's what... I've had it ever since I woke up here. Tried to toss it, but no matter what I do, it always reappears. Such a pain...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Anyway, if any of you want the "Hero's Sword," you can have it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... It's called what?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: The "Hero's Sword," meant to be wielded by the hero... I know, me of all people, right? The irony.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? ...YOU'RE the Hero of this world?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Will you calm down? It's just a dumb title.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh... It's just that, this entire time, we thought we were the heroes of the prophecy...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Well, if it means that much to you, you're welcome to claim the title. You'd be doing me a favor.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm good, actually...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not the point... The real question is: If you're the hero, then where the heck have you been all this time?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Looking for a way out.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I heard there's a boat in this area that can bring you to another world, so I came to investigate.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: But look at the state of things around here — the lighthouse collapsed, the boat won't budge... I say we try to find a different way out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Paimon's guessing a voice told you what you were supposed to do here... That's what happened with Navia and Nilou, at least.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hah, you expect me to take orders from some disembodied voice?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, wait! Where are you going?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: To find the so-called "source of this world's misfortune" — the dragon responsible for this whole mess.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wait, we came here to fight the dragon as well. Why don't we go together?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: ...Tch. Grab that <color=#00E1FFFF>dragon scale</color> over there before you leave. It'll come in handy later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A dragon scale? Where? How did you know about it? What's it for? And—

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Have you ever considered keeping your questions to yourself? Because if you actually expect me to answer them all, we'll be here until the next Interdarshan Championship.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You little...! Ugh, Paimon thought you might've learned some manners by now, but clearly not!

choices.text: But it seemed like someone was talking in my head just now.

talks.objective: Look for the dragon scale
Look for the dragon scale
Obtain the dragon scale

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we made it.. But, with the force of this waterfall, there's no way we're getting through!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Quick, take out the dragon scale.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but... No, Paimon doesn't need to ask you anything! Hmm... The dragon scale can turn anything it touches into toy blocks, so... Aha! You want to use it to block off the water!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See! Paimon can figure things out all on her own!

talks.objective: Talk to everyone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should do it, right? Wow, this scale is amazing! It turns everything it touches into something hard, almost like a toy block. Doesn't seem to work on us, though.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It spews out poison, and transmutes everything it touches... No wonder they call it the "evil dragon."

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Your Majesty! Madame Fairy! Brave Hero!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What are you looking at me for? He's obviously talking to you.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Mr. Wheel! You didn't get hurt when we fell, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: No, not at all. Thankfully, the young man in the hat was kind enough to lend me a hand.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Tch...

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: There seems to be a village over here. Some of the residents used to work in the toytanium mines, and some came to fight the dragon, then got stuck here.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I see... I'm glad they're all safe and sound. I can try to use my magic to fold a boat to bring everyone back.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'll help, too! Still, I think we need to take care of the dragon first. We don't want it to start causing trouble when we're trying to load people onto the ship.

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Apparently, the villagers often see the dragon fly into <color=#00E1FFFF>a space behind the waterfall</color>. They think that's the location of its lair.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, we should look around and try to find a way in!

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: I'll wait here for your triumphant return. Your Majesty, brave heroes... Please, be careful.

talks.objective: Go near the waterfall where the fell dragon resides
Go near the waterfall where the fell dragon resides
Use the dragon scale to enter the waterfall

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Nilou?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, nothing. It's just... I sensed a very powerful magical signature just now...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Guess this is the dragon's lair after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? When did you put your hat on?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, we're getting ready to fight, aren't we? I feel more comfortable in my regular outfit. Hat Guy also put away that sword around his waist.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Should've never had the useless thing to begin with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Do... Do you need to do anything to prepare, {NICKNAME}? Paimon's getting kinda nervous, seeing everyone all serious like this.

choices.text: I just need a little longer...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Of course! We should be fully prepared before going in.

talks.objective: Use the dragon scale to enter the waterfall

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm good. Let's go.

talks.objective: Explore the space within the waterfall
Explore the space within the waterfall

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Well? How long are you gonna keep us waiting?

choices.text: I just need a little longer...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Of course! We should be fully prepared before going in.

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Huh, this space is completely empty...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon bets this is where the dragon sleeps...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! The road behind us is cut off!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Watch out in front! It's coming!

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair
Go deep within the fell dragon's lair
Go deep within the fell dragon's lair
Listen to the voice near your ear

dialogues.speaker: Voice of a Woman
dialogues.text: Look. He's here.

dialogues.speaker: Voice of Another Woman
dialogues.text: Ah... Another new soul has joined this world.

dialogues.speaker: Voice of a Woman
dialogues.text: But... Are you sure his fate will be as you described?

dialogues.speaker: Voice of Another Woman
dialogues.text: Of course. My predictions are never wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Voice of a Woman
dialogues.text: I just don't like that kind of story...

dialogues.speaker: Voice of Another Woman
dialogues.text: Then you need only do as you said, and let him find his own story within your fairytale.

dialogues.speaker: Voice of a Woman
dialogues.text: Haha, you're right. Then, listen closely, my child. Your name is—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that... water?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Are we above Constellation Metropole?

dialogues.speaker: City Resident
dialogues.text: It's... It's the dragon! The dragon that destroyed the toytanium mines!

dialogues.speaker: City Resident
dialogues.text: Help!! Heeeeeelp!!!

dialogues.speaker: "Capital Guard"
dialogues.text: Soldiers, pick up your weapons! Destroy that monster!

talks.objective: Listen out for the voice near your ear
Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Ugh. How many times am I going to have to save you?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Thank you, Hat Guy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Paimon still feels dizzy... Hey, did any of you also see something strange? It was like we were witnessing...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: The dragon's memories?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Sounds like we all saw the same thing just now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we definitely saw a different side to the story... Watching it all unfold, Paimon couldn't help but feel bad for the dragon...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: This world might be a lot more complicated than we thought.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The next time we encounter the dragon, how about we try talking to him instead of fighting?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds like a good plan... But, maybe we should figure out where we ended up first...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hm, if the world above is a fairytale realm, then maybe we've fallen into the next page of the book...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Just keep walking, and don't fall behind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Hey! Wait for us!

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair
Go deep within the fell dragon's lair
Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: ...Hat Guy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're getting too far away!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He's just up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Is he trying to lure us somewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well... I'd say we were the ones who backed him into a corner...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... we just wanna ask him a few questions about his past...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He's had year after year of people coming here to try to take his head. If you ask me, his reaction is perfectly normal.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Maybe there's still something we can do to calm him down!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I wouldn't count on it. Maybe his earlier attacks were just a warning, but now, he's actually getting serious.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Prepare for a final battle. Sometimes... it takes a little force for someone to finally wake up.

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair
Go deep within the fell dragon's lair
Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now's our chance!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...! Wait!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Huh...!

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: Voice of a Woman
dialogues.text: Are you sure you want to create this child, M, even after what I told you about his fate?

dialogues.speaker: Voice of a Woman
dialogues.text: He will be abandoned by his creator, and eventually...

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: I know, B. You've told me already. That sad story with the disappointing ending... It's what happened in the real world, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: But, that's exactly why I want to change things. In a different world, his story can have a happier ending. That child... His heart is so full of love.

dialogues.speaker: "B"
dialogues.text: I understand, Anya. But, know that if you give him that name, his fate in Simulanka is destined to parallel that of his real-world namesake...

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: But, there's still a chance, right? Maybe it's a shot in the dark... But, I have to try. He deserves a better life.

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: Although... he might need the help of others when the time comes.

dialogues.speaker: "B"
dialogues.text: Alright, my dear, the choice is yours.

dialogues.speaker: "B"
dialogues.text: Since you're so persistent, let me tell you a secret...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hmph... More boring "fate" talk.

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair
Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, my child...

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: Unlike my friends, I don't have a long time to live. All said and done, the story of my life will be shorter than the fairy tales in this book. So, I will have to leave your side, I'm afraid.

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: It's okay, it's okay. Once I'm gone, I will become a star in Simulanka, and watch over you from above. If you ever feel lonely, just look up towards the sky...

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: Go forth and witness this world, my child... Make sure to be nice to everyone...

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: You'll meet good friends one day, I'm sure of it... That is my wish for your future.

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: As for this world... I leave it to you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So, in the end, you were "betrayed," too...

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: Little Flying Squirrel
dialogues.text: Hey, mister dragon! I brought you some food. You must be hungry?

dialogues.speaker: Little Flying Squirrel
dialogues.text: Shh...! Quiet, we can't let anyone hear us. Everyone says you're a bad dragon, but you're always nice to me when we play together. You always help me pick the flowers way up high that I can't reach.

dialogues.speaker: Little Flying Squirrel
dialogues.text: It's okay. Just keep hiding here, and tomorrow, I'll—

dialogues.speaker: Flying Squirrel Mama
dialogues.text: Oh no! My child!

dialogues.speaker: Flying Squirrel Mama
dialogues.text: Help, somebody help me! Save my child, the dragon's trying to kidnap her!

dialogues.speaker: Little Flying Squirrel
dialogues.text: No! Mom, it's not like that! Listen to me...!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So, you're hated by people, too...

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So, that's it? That's really your wish?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: "To never have been born at all"... That's not a fate you should wish for.

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That was a close call! Are you guys alright?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yup, all thanks to Kirara.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Back in Constellation Metropole, I heard people saying you'd gone to fight the dragon, so I followed you here. Right when I managed to catch up, I saw you fall through that hole!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Wait, didn't someone else fall through just now? Shouldn't we do something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah, Hat Guy... Well, he can fly, so he'll probably be fine...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: He called the dragon something earlier. It sounded like he said...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Durin. That's his name.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hat Guy, you're okay! Wait, what about the dragon... Durin?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He's fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Durin... Wait, that's the name of the dragon from Dragonspine, right? The one that became a part of the mountain after being slain by Dvalin! If Paimon remembers correctly, it was created by...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Gold" Rhinedottir...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, it was created by Rhinedottir.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Created, you say... Heh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what exactly happened down there? You've been acting weird ever since the end of the fight!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: #{REALNAME[ID(1)]} tells you about what he saw in the mist...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: So that's the truth about Simulanka's evil dragon...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What we saw in the mist weren't hallucinations, but the dragon's memories...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Everything I heard during my fall... must have been things said to Durin in the past...)

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Huh, I thought it was strange! The people around the Broken Sea are clearly stranded, but I never heard any stories about the dragon attacking the village.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The people we met along the way are probably workers from the toytanium mines, or guards who came here to claim the dragon's head... Durin probably allowed them to live here because there was nowhere else for them to go...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: When I first came to this world, a voice spoke to me and said, "You are the Hero of this world. Now go forth, and save the dragon."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, who is the person behind this voice, anyway? And why did they bring us all here?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Come with me. The answer to all of this can be found below.

talks.objective: Go deep within the fell dragon's lair
Go deep within the fell dragon's lair

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Is this... a study?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: That's right. It belongs to the Goddess of Fate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Goddess of Fate? As in, one of the three Goddesses who created Simulanka?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Or more precisely, "M." One of the Mages of the Hexenzirkel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hexenzirkel!? As in...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Sorry, Paimon shouldn't just regurgitate everything you say. It's just... it's a lot to take in.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: She created the story of Durin. Well, the Simulanka version, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: These records should cover most of what you want to know, including the identities of the other two Goddesses. Read them for yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Old Journal
dialogues.text: "...By all rights, I should have been 'A,' since 'A' is the first and last letter of my name. But Alice overruled me on the basis of seniority, and said I would be 'M' instead, because of my middle name. Haha, she really knows how to push my buttons..."

dialogues.speaker: Old Journal
dialogues.text: "Still, her magic never fails to amaze me. I still can't believe she got one of my origami frogs to start talking."

dialogues.speaker: Old Journal
dialogues.text: "Hmm... Why don't I write a story with origami animals as the main characters? Let's see... Once upon a time, in a magical Forest, there lived a group of animals made of paper..."

dialogues.speaker: Old Journal
dialogues.text: "Barbie loves looking into the future, so she used her powers to map out the fates of all living things in Simulanka. But knowing the ending in advance takes all the fun out of the story..."

dialogues.speaker: Old Journal
dialogues.text: "I think I'll make a bet with her. I believe that one day, the people of Simulanka will decide to carve their own destiny."

dialogues.speaker: Old Journal
dialogues.text: "...Apparently, she wants to build a statue of herself in the capital city!? Haha, always looking to add some pizzazz."

dialogues.speaker: Yellowed Letter
dialogues.text: "My dear sisters, I fear my pen shall soon run dry... Even now as I write this letter to you, my dexterity is all but failing me. Thank you for enjoying my stories, and for creating this world for me..."

dialogues.speaker: Yellowed Letter
dialogues.text: "The time we spent together was the most wonderful youth I could have asked for. Haha, I always feel so young when we're together..."

dialogues.speaker: Yellowed Letter
dialogues.text: "'A' says that even after I am gone, the Goddess of Fate in Simulanka will continue to exist, and carry on granting people's wishes. It makes me glad..."

dialogues.speaker: Yellowed Letter
dialogues.text: "If you ever want to chat, feel free to pay a visit to the Goddess statue. Just don't wish for anything weird!"

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's... Simulanka Durin? And he's looking up at something... a star.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: This must have been after M passed away...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That statue looks different from the one in the Metropole.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's a different goddess. This one is the Goddess of Fate.

dialogues.text: Ta-da! Surprise, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah! A talking street lamp!
Street lamp...? Oh my, you mean you still don't remember me, after all the times we've spoken?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I know that voice... It's Mom's friend!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alice.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: #Hello there, {NICKNAME} and friends. And Durin — it's good to see you. You've changed quite a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: In fact, you look so different that perhaps... I should call you "Mini Durin"?

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: "Mini Durin," huh... Yeah, I like the sound of that! It's nice being smaller.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You must be one of the three Goddesses of this world... Are you the Goddess of Creation?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Yep, that's right! But although it's the most impressive-sounding of the three, to be honest, we all made an equal contribution toward the founding of this world.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: If you've ever read any of M's stories, you'll know just how enchanting the worlds are that she writes about. So enchanting that I just had to step inside and explore it for real.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: So I got B involved, and with M's consent, created the world of Simulanka.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa whoa whoa, you're getting a little ahead of yourself! First things first, would you mind explaining what you're doing here? ...In fact, no, what are WE even doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Haha, don't worry! All will be revealed! After everything you accomplished on your journey, you're free to ask me anything you want.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hm, let's start with your first question, then. I'm here because I sensed a great magic power emanating from the book just now, and I couldn't resist the urge to peek inside and check it out.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That must have been when we all gave Mini Durin our blessings, right?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Yes, exactly. In the world of fairytales, words and emotions often carry far more power than any spell.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to your magic that Mini Durin was able to take this form. Come say hi to me, little one. Ah, look at you. You're as cute as a button!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: So... What about us? Was it always part of the plan that we'd come here?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: "Plan" isn't the word I'd use. If you ask me, I'd say... fate works in mysterious ways.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: When Durin of Simulanka made his wish to the Goddess of Fate, it just so happened that in a world far away, all of you wonderful people were holding a copy of M's fairytale at that exact moment.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: And because of your noble and kind souls, you were selected by the Goddess of Fate to come and save this world.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Now that you mention it... That's what I was doing when I was transported here! I was reading a fairytale to some children in the Fleuve Cendre!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I think I just... happened upon an old book, and decided to use it as my pillow during a nap in a box... Hehehe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... What a crazy coincidence...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that's not right... How come everyone else got assigned a role except us? 'Cause we were also...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Yeah, that was it! We'd just received a strange book, and we had no idea who sent it. Then, the moment we opened it up to start reading it, we found ourselves here... You're the one who sent it to us, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Oh, is that what happened? Hahaha, yes, that does sound like me, doesn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why did you send us here?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hmm... Good question. Why, indeed? Maybe I thought this was such a good story, it simply had to be read by someone. As the Traveler and witness of many worlds, how could I let such a beautiful place pass you by?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: I can sense that your blessing for Mini Durin was a very special one. With this blessing from beyond the story, he might even be able to explore worlds outside of this one.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Teyvat, you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: That's right. In fact, back when we were first creating Simulanka, M told us that she hoped the people of this world would one day be able to explore the wider world beyond.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: "Every story has an ending, but if the story becomes reality, it should have the right to choose its own path."

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So in other words... the predestined lives these people lead were always going to disappear one way or another.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so if even the people here get to go to other worlds... Surely there's gotta be a way we can leave, too, right?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Don't you realize you've been able to leave all along?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: You can either take the <color=#00E1FFFF>boat</color> at the Broken Sea, or touch the <color=#00E1FFFF>giant bookmark</color> at the Cliff of Prophecy. All you need to do if you want to leave is focus on the place you want to go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...How were we supposed to know that if you never told us!?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Huh? Didn't I? Hehe, well, given how smart and capable you are, surely that can't have posed a huge problem for you?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: As for your other friends who were summoned here... If I had to guess, I'd say the Goddess of Fate probably didn't tell them about it because she wanted them to get engrossed in the story.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: She's M's reflection, after all. It wouldn't surprise me if she shares M's love for cliffhangers!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Anyway, I think that answers your questions, yes? What do you all plan to do next?

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: I... I'm gonna go say sorry to the people of this world. After that... I wanna start protecting Simulanka, just like Mom told me to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Now we know how easy it is to get back home, Paimon's suddenly not in such a hurry to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Same here! It's not every day that you get to come to such a magical world. I, for one, plan to explore it a little longer.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Haha, I'm glad to hear it. Maybe I should invite some other friends to join you, too...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: By the way, Mini Durin, I'm delighted to see you've made some new friends. I'm sure M would be very proud of you.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Now, before I depart, please let me give you a blessing as well. May your future be as rich and colorful as the stories M used to tell.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: ...She's gone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess this is where the Hero's journey comes to an end, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh, but it's also where a new journey begins: The adventures of Mini Durin and friends!

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: Huh? An adventure for me...?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You bet! For starters, I'd love to introduce you to my other friends in the Forest. Even though there have been some misunderstandings in the past, I'm sure they'll welcome the new you with open arms.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Stop looking at me. I already said I'll come with you!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Whoa! Look over there!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Wow... The stars are beautiful...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'll bet that's a gift to Mini Durin from the three Goddesses of this world!

dialogues.speaker: Mini Durin
dialogues.text: Thank you, Mom...

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Nobody can define who you are...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Or deny the true feelings of your heart

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Now, remember your name—

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Durin

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's alright now...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: This looks like... a mine.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Maybe... the toytanium miners dug too deep? So deep that they dug right through to the world on the next page?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Yeah... Now that you mention it, this miner's lamp looks really similar to the star on the previous page...

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The Forest of Blessings... This book has been recording Simulanka's history all along...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Look at the size of those footprints... If that's every time he lands, then no wonder people are so terrified of him.

dialogues.text: As the ground beneath your feet crumbles away, you feel a sense of weightlessness as you fall into the black mist below...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The time has come to slay the dragon! How are you feeling? Nervous?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's curious to see what this "end of the world" place is like. C'mon, let's go meet the others at the station.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Are we... inside the black mist?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Huh? I see something up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: The book's on the move again.
